page: OVHcloud t2-le-180 is a cloud GPU server instance configured on a KVM hypervisor, engineered for parallelized computational workflows and machine learning. The server is powered by Intel Xeon 6226R processors running on the x86_64 architecture, providing 60 dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz. CPU instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512 (f and vnni), and AES cryptography flags. Memory capacity is fixed at 180.0 GB of system RAM, allocating 3.0 GB per core. Acceleration hardware comprises 4 NVIDIA Volta V100S GPUs providing a total pool of 128 GB VRAM. The instance also provisions 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network connection, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional machine learning acceleration alongside consistent multi-core processing throughput. In large language model inference, the quad V100S array demonstrates top-tier performance, delivering 15,284.46 prompt tokens per second and 278.47 generation tokens per second on a small 135M model, alongside 1,277.99 prompt tokens per second and 120.29 generation tokens per second on a 7B model. CPU throughput exhibits solid mid-to-high capabilities, registering a PassMark CPU score of 42,630.35 and PassMark extended instructions score of 52,461.06 in the top quartile. Memory access benchmarks show uncached large-block reads of 116.96 GB/sec and uncached writes of 41.01 GB/sec. Data processing tasks reflect strong multithreaded capacity, with bzip3 decompression achieving 311.42 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure perspective, the t2-le-180 offers balanced multi-GPU hardware density suitable for distributed training, deep learning inference, high-performance computing (HPC) simulations, and complex computer vision tasks. While the local NVMe capacity is modest at 500 GB relative to the heavy compute profile, the 10 Gbps baseline network pipeline facilitates integration with remote block and object storage pools. The server is an effective fit for parallelized machine learning models up to 7B parameters, scientific modeling, batch transcoding, and vector-intensive compute jobs.
